reviewBoundary: Four complete junior ten-gap passages. Fictional newspaper/class/subtitle/weather-club cases, qualified measurement descriptions. Same-author variant and invalid-form review only, not independent calibration.

units.title: A correction in the school paper
units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage with seven supplied-word and three one-word gaps. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: A correction in the school paper
materials.text:
Our school newspaper published a report about the swimming team last month. On the next morning, a team member ____1____ (notice) that one result was wrong. The article said her team had finished second, but it had actually finished third.

The editor thanked her ____2____ pointing it out. He checked the official results before changing anything. The team member was right, and the error had come from an early version of the writer's notes.

At first, the editor wanted to replace the number ____3____ (quiet). Our teacher suggested adding a short correction note instead. Readers ____4____ had already seen the wrong version needed to know what had changed.

The note explained the mistake without blaming the student who reported it. It also gave the correct result. The team was disappointed about not finishing second, but its members preferred an accurate report to ____5____ false success.

The corrected page ____6____ (share) with the team that afternoon. Several students wrote back to say thank you. The editor kept a copy of both ____7____ (version) in the newspaper's records, clearly marking which one had been corrected.

Before ____8____ (publish) the next sports report, the writers checked their notes against the final results. The extra step took a little time, but it was ____9____ (easy) than explaining another avoidable error. The first mistake had not made ____10____ (they) newspaper useless. It had shown where the checking process needed to improve.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of notice.
questions.explanation: The report and next morning form a past narrative, so noticed. Base and unaided -ing forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Thanked her for pointing it out takes for. Other listed prepositions do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of quiet.
questions.explanation: Quietly modifies replace. Quietness is a noun; unlisted informal uses stay reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Readers are the human subject antecedent of who/that had seen. Which is nonhuman, where not subject and whose needs a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A false success begins with consonant f. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of share.
questions.explanation: Singular page receives sharing, so was/had been shared. Shared alone lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of version.
questions.explanation: Both requires plural versions. Singular or singular possessive does not name the two copies.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of publish.
questions.explanation: Before publishing takes -ing after a preposition. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of easy.
questions.explanation: Than gives comparative easier/more easy. Easiest is superlative and more easier doubled.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of they.
questions.explanation: Their modifies newspaper. Personal pronouns and independent theirs do not fit before the noun.

units.title: Two sides of a balance
units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage with seven supplied-word and three one-word gaps. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: Two sides of a balance
materials.text:
In science class, we used a simple balance to compare objects. Our teacher put a small bag on one side and asked us ____1____ (find) objects that would balance it on the other. We were not allowed to open the bag yet.

I chose three wooden blocks. The bag's side stayed lower, so I added another block. My partner watched ____2____ (careful) and asked whether the balance had been level before we started. We had forgotten to check.

After ____3____ (remove) everything, we saw that one pan still hung lower. The teacher helped us adjust the equipment. Only then did we begin our comparison again. A fair result needed more ____4____ a confident guess about the objects.

This time, five blocks balanced the bag. Another group used several metal washers instead. Their answer did not disagree with ours simply ____5____ the number of objects was different. The washers and blocks were not the same mass.

We wrote a description ____6____ explained exactly what we had compared. Then the teacher opened the bag. It contained a small toy car, not the stones I had imagined.

The activity was ____7____ (use) because it made us separate two questions: what an object was and how its mass compared with another's. My notebook showed two different ____8____ (result), with the comparison objects named clearly. The balance ____9____ (check) again before the next class used it. We had learned to examine ____10____ (we) starting point as well as the final answer.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of find.
questions.explanation: Asked us takes to find. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies watched. Careful is adjective and carefulness noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of remove.
questions.explanation: After removing/having removed expresses the prior action. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: More than means beyond merely a guess. Then is time and that does not complete the comparison.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Because/as/since introduce the rejected simple reason: a different item count alone does not establish disagreement. Unless reverses that logic.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Description is subject antecedent of that/which explained. Who is human, where not subject and what conflicts with the antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of use.
questions.explanation: Useful describes the activity. Use is noun/verb and usefully adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of result.
questions.explanation: Two different results explicitly requires the plural. Singular result and singular possessive result’s do not fill that plural count slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: The singular balance receives checking. Was/had been checked fit the past sequence; checked lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Our modifies starting point. Personal and independent possessive forms do not directly modify it.

units.title: Reading the moving words
units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage with seven supplied-word and three one-word gaps. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: Reading the moving words
materials.text:
Our media club made a short video with subtitles for a school project. At first, we simply copied the spoken words and placed them at the bottom of the screen. We soon found that ____1____ (read) those words while watching the action was harder than reading them on paper.

Some lines remained on screen for only a moment. Others covered part of the image ____2____ viewers needed to see. The subtitles were technically present, but that did not mean they were easy to use.

A teacher asked us to watch without sound. We missed an important change of speaker because two people were outside the frame. We added a short label ____3____ (identify) the new voice where the picture did not make it clear.

We also divided long sentences into ____4____ (short) units. This was not permission to change the meaning. We compared the edited lines with the recording to check that necessary information had not disappeared.

Before ____5____ (finish), we showed the video to classmates who had not helped make it. Their questions revealed places where our ____6____ (familiar) with the story had hidden a problem. We knew what would happen next; a new viewer did not.

The revised video ____7____ (display) at the school meeting. Afterwards, we kept the subtitle file with the final recording so that the two could be updated together. A correction to one version without a change ____8____ the other could create a new mismatch. The project gave ____9____ (we) a practical understanding of access. Adding words was only ____10____ beginning; making them usable required attention to timing, context and meaning.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of read.
questions.explanation: Reading or to read can form the subject of was. Read/reads are finite/base forms that do not directly fill this nominal subject slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Part of the image that/which viewers needed to see supplies the object relative. Who is human, where locative and what incompatible with the antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of identify.
questions.explanation: To identify states the label’s purpose; identifying the new voice is also a participial modifier of label. Base and finite past do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of short.
questions.explanation: Shorter/more short expresses reduction relative to long sentences. Shortest is superlative and more shorter doubled; unlisted plain adjective remains reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of finish.
questions.explanation: Before finishing takes an -ing clause after the preposition. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of familiar.
questions.explanation: Our familiarity with the story requires a noun. Familiar is adjective and familiarly adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of display.
questions.explanation: Singular video receives display in this past narrative. Displayed alone lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A change to/in the other refers to updating that version. From would suggest changing away from it rather than correcting its content; other unlisted readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Gave takes object us. Subject and possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The beginning identifies the first stage; a beginning is also grammatical as an initial step. An before consonant b is invalid.

units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage with seven supplied-word and three one-word gaps. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: Where the rain gauge stood
materials.text:
The school weather club put a rain gauge in the garden and recorded the water collected after each rainy day. For a week, our numbers were much lower than those from a nearby school. We wondered whether our garden ____1____ (receive) less rain.

Our teacher asked where the gauge stood. It was beside a wall, under the edge of a tree. We had chosen the spot because it was convenient ____2____ (reach), without considering how the surroundings could affect collection.

Leaves could intercept some water, while drips from a branch might add water in a different way. We needed a site ____3____ allowed a more representative collection, not simply a container that was easy to visit.

Following appropriate local measurement guidance, we moved the gauge and checked that it was level. We wrote the change of site in our record instead of ____4____ (hide) it. Otherwise, someone reading the numbers later might assume that every observation had been made under the same ____5____ (condition).

The next readings were closer to those from the neighbouring school, but the two sets were not identical. The gauges were still in different places, and small local differences were possible. We were ____6____ (careful) than before about treating one difference as proof of an error.

At the end of term, our report included ____7____ explanation of the first site and the date it changed. Our teacher thanked ____8____ (we) for keeping that detail. A method change was part ____9____ the evidence, not an embarrassing mark to erase. The experience helped us judge the numbers more ____10____ (accurate), while recognising that a school project was not a complete weather-monitoring service.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of receive.
questions.explanation: Past simple/progressive/perfect all fit the uncertain comparison in the past. Receiving alone lacks a finite auxiliary; other tense readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of reach.
questions.explanation: Convenient to reach uses an infinitive. Other listed forms do not directly complete that adjective construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Site is subject antecedent of that/which allowed. Where would lack a subject and who/what do not fit this nonhuman expressed antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of hide.
questions.explanation: Instead of takes hiding. Other listed forms do not directly follow the preposition.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of condition.
questions.explanation: The same conditions names the collection circumstances. Conditional is adjective; singular condition is left reviewable because it can name an overall state.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Than gives comparative more careful; rare carefuller is allowed. Most is superlative and more carefuller doubled.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An explanation begins with a vowel sound. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Thanked takes object us. Subject and possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Part of the evidence takes of. Other listed prepositions do not express inclusion.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of accurate.
questions.explanation: Accurately modifies judge. Accurate is adjective and accuracy noun.
